title: Stir-Fried Tomato and Scrambled Eggs
summary: Soft egg curds set in a hot wok, then folded into tomatoes stir-fried with garlic, ginger and spring onion and cooked until the eggs are fully set.
equipment: wok or large non-stick frying pan

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
spring onions, whites chopped, greens sliced
ripe plum tomatoes, cut into 2.5 cm wedges
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Scramble the eggs
steps.text: Whisk the eggs with 1/4 tsp salt and the water. Heat the wok over high heat, add 2 tbsp oil, pour in the eggs and turn the heat down to medium-low. Let a layer set underneath before pushing the egg into large soft curds, 2-3 min; tip onto a plate and wipe the wok. The water turns to steam as they cook, making the curds lighter.

steps.title: Fry the aromatics
steps.text: Heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil over medium-high heat. Stir-fry the spring onion whites and garlic for about 20 seconds, then add the ginger for 10 seconds more, keeping everything moving so nothing scorches.

steps.title: Cook the tomatoes
steps.text: Add the tomatoes with 1/2 tsp salt and the sugar and stir-fry for 3-4 min, until they soften and their juices bubble into a light sauce. The salt draws out the juices, and the sugar rounds off their acidity.

steps.title: Fold and finish
steps.text: Return the eggs with the white pepper and cook for 2-3 min, breaking up any very large curds, until the eggs are fully set (71 °C) and everything is hot. Off the heat, stir in the sesame oil and spring onion greens, then serve with rice.

tips: Use the ripest tomatoes you can find; underripe ones give a thin, sharp sauce.
A common mistake is crowding a cool pan, which makes the eggs rubbery; get the wok properly hot first.
Taste the sauce before adding the eggs back and add a pinch more sugar if the tomatoes are very tart.
Canned whole tomatoes, drained and chunked, work out of season.
storage: Best eaten fresh. Refrigerate covered up to 2 days and reheat in a pan or microwave until piping hot (74 °C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
